problemStatement: People create short links to malicious destinations. Refuse links to blocklisted domains and to other URL shorteners (whose final destination these checks cannot see) when they are created, and let an admin flag an existing abusive link so that it stops redirecting (451). No external reputation API and no rescan of existing links.

functional.text: Creating a link whose destination host is a blocklisted domain, or a subdomain of one, is refused with 400 invalid-url and reason BLOCKED_DOMAIN. The blocklist is configuration (shortener.abuse.blocked-domains), matched case-insensitively.

Creating a link to another URL shortener (bit.ly, tinyurl.com, t.co and other listed shortener domains, or subdomains of them) is refused with 400 invalid-url and reason URL_SHORTENER; the list is configuration (shortener.abuse.shortener-domains) with the common public shorteners as its default.
An admin can flag a link with POST /api/v1/admin/links/{code}/flag (204, idempotent); only API keys named in shortener.abuse.admin-keys may, others get 403 forbidden.
A flagged link answers 451 with type /problems/link-unavailable on redirect, from the next request on, even if it was cached.
The owner sees a flagged link with status FLAGGED; unknown and deleted links cannot be flagged (404).

nonFunctional.text: The checks add no network call: the blocklist is matched in memory and the redirect path is unchanged for active links.
Every flag is logged with the admin key that set it.

acceptanceCriteria.when: links to https://evil.test/login and https://www.EVIL.test/x are created
a link to https://notevil.test/ is created
acceptanceCriteria.then: 201: a suffix is not a subdomain

acceptanceCriteria.when: links to https://bit.ly/abc, https://t.co/y and https://go.bit.ly/z are created
acceptanceCriteria.then: 400 invalid-url with reason URL_SHORTENER; a link to this service itself stays SELF_REFERENCE

acceptanceCriteria.given: a key that is not an admin key
acceptanceCriteria.then: 403 forbidden and the link still redirects; 401 without a key

acceptanceCriteria.given: a link that has redirected once (cached)
acceptanceCriteria.when: an admin flags it and GET /{code}
acceptanceCriteria.then: 451 link-unavailable, on every later request too

acceptanceCriteria.given: an unknown or a deleted link

assumptions: Admins are API keys listed by name; there is no separate admin login.
A flagged link stays FLAGGED; unflagging is out of scope.
The cross-instance L1 window of BF-1 also applies to flags: other instances may redirect a just-flagged link for up to the L1 TTL.
